# `data/stale-deps-snapshot`

**The dependency snapshot is recent**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-data` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-data` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JSON, TOML |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:data/package-json` at `info` · `codelaw:data/pyproject` at `info` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `info` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (refreshing the snapshot reads the registries, which needs the network; the engine never uses it (L5)) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Files** | only `package.json`, `pyproject.toml` |

## What it checks

`.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json` — the registry facts `data/outdated-dependency` reads — was fetched no more than `[deps] max_snapshot_age` (14 days by default) before the as-of date, and can be read. The finding is on the root `package.json`, or the root `pyproject.toml` when there is no root `package.json`, so a project gets one. The age is judged on the as-of date (`--as-of`, `CODELAW_AS_OF`, else `HEAD`'s commit date), never the clock; with no as-of date, only an unreadable snapshot is reported.

**Why:** An old snapshot hides every release since it was written, so `data/outdated-dependency` says a dependency is current when it isn't.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-data
pip install codelaw-rules-data
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:data/package-json` sets it to `info`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:data/package-json"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"data/stale-deps-snapshot" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.json"]
rules = { "data/stale-deps-snapshot" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"data/stale-deps-snapshot" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"data/stale-deps-snapshot" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"data/stale-deps-snapshot" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "data/stale-deps-snapshot": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Also configured by `[deps]`

The dependency rules, `data/outdated-dependency` and `data/stale-deps-snapshot`, read against `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, which `codelaw deps refresh` writes (SR-RULE-PACKS decision 15). Root config only.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[deps.severity]` | table | — | The severity of each kind of finding, or `off`: a major, minor or patch version behind, a deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI) version in use, a lockfile behind a range that allows the latest. |
| `severity.major` | `error` · `warn` · `info` · `off` | `"warn"` |  |
| `severity.minor` | `error` · `warn` · `info` · `off` | `"info"` |  |
| `severity.patch` | `error` · `warn` · `info` · `off` | `"info"` |  |
| `severity.deprecated` | `error` · `warn` · `info` · `off` | `"error"` |  |
| `severity.yanked` | `error` · `warn` · `info` · `off` | `"error"` |  |
| `severity.lockfile` | `error` · `warn` · `info` · `off` | `"info"` |  |
| `min_release_age` | `integer or string` | `0` | Releases younger than this on the snapshot's `fetched` date are not offered: days, or a string like "7d" or "2w". |
| `prerelease` | `boolean` | `false` | Offer prereleases. `deps refresh` keeps them in the snapshot only when this is on. |
| `ignore` | `array` | — | Packages never reported: `npm:<name>` or `pypi:<name>`, or a table with `package` and an `expires` date (the first day it no longer holds), `added_by` and `reason`. |
| `max_snapshot_age` | `integer or string` | `14` | A snapshot older than this on the as-of date is `data/stale-deps-snapshot`: days, or a string like "14d". |

```toml
[deps]
min_release_age = "7d"
prerelease = false
max_snapshot_age = 14
ignore = ["npm:left-pad", { package = "pypi:requests", expires = "2027-01-01", added_by = "you@example.com", reason = "pinned until the client upgrade" }]

[deps.severity]
major = "warn"
minor = "info"
patch = "off"
deprecated = "error"
yanked = "error"
lockfile = "info"
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JSON** has no comments: switch the rule off for the file with a scope, or use the baseline.
- **TOML:** `# codelaw-ignore data/stale-deps-snapshot: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `# codelaw-ignore data/stale-deps-snapshot expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule data/stale-deps-snapshot --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain data/stale-deps-snapshot       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule data/stale-deps-snapshot  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>            # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Run `codelaw deps refresh`: it reads npm and the Python index and writes the snapshot again.
2. Commit `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, so CI and every teammate judge by the same facts.

## Examples

### JSON

#### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": [ }
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

#### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": {} }
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

### TOML

#### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": [ }
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```

#### Do

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": {} }
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```
